title: Deployment scorecard + sprint backlog for customer POC
content:
Purpose and audience:
Quick working doc for the payments-cust POC decision workshop (9/11). Audience: SEs, infra PM, customer engineering lead. Outcome: pick a minimal, low-risk deployment path for a 6-week POC that demonstrates latency, cost, and compliance tradeoffs.

High-level customer constraints (copied from discovery):
- Industry: mid-market payments processor (PCI scope).
- Data: customer-side tokens + some sensitive metadata; cannot send full card data off their VPC.
- Expected POC throughput: 150 requests/minute peak, mostly short sequences (prompt ~200 tokens total).
- SLO target: p95 < 180ms for single-turn predictive scoring; batch/async allowed for non-real-time tasks.
- Budget: limited; prefers predictable monthly commit if possible.

Immediate ask to SE workshop: decide recommended POC path (hosted / dedicated / private / hybrid), list engineering tasks for the POC sprint, produce a one-page cost delta and a short risk register.

SCORECARD (qualitative + quick numerical heuristics)
Columns: Criteria | Hosted | Dedicated | Private
- Latency (p95): Hosted = 120–220ms (depends on region & cold starts). Dedicated = 90–150ms (reserved GPUs, tuned). Private = 80–140ms (on-prem or VPC with local infra).
- Cost predictability: Hosted = low (usage var + per-token) ; Dedicated = high (commit); Private = high (capex/Opex opaque).
- Compliance / Data residency: Hosted = medium (SaaS with contractual controls) ; Dedicated = high (isolated pools + contractual controls); Private = very high (customer-controlled infra).
- Deployment lead time: Hosted = <1 day to sign + API keys; Dedicated = 2–4 weeks; Private = 4–8 weeks (depends on customer infra readiness).
- Ops overhead (customer + Redwood): Hosted = minimal; Dedicated = moderate (we manage pool, customer monitors); Private = high (customer infra + SE setup).
- Rollout flexibility (canaries/model pinning): Hosted = good (fast model swaps); Dedicated = very good; Private = depends on site ops but possible.
- Fallback options during outage: Hosted = auto-fallback to lower-cap models; Dedicated = fallback to hosted or spare pool; Private = requires pre-negotiated fallback (we should define).

Quick numeric scoring (0–5, higher = better)
- Latency: Hosted 3, Dedicated 4, Private 4
- Predictability: Hosted 2, Dedicated 5, Private 4
- Compliance: Hosted 3, Dedicated 4, Private 5
- Time-to-demo: Hosted 5, Dedicated 3, Private 1
- Ops burden (lower is better -> invert to score): Hosted 5, Dedicated 3, Private 2

Score totals: Hosted 18, Dedicated 19, Private 16 -> Recommendation leans to Dedicated for this POC, with a staged hybrid fallback to Hosted for burst and Private only if customer can commit to infra timeline. Rationale: Dedicated balances latency, compliance, and predictable costs while keeping demo velocity reasonable.

Recommended POC approach (staged-hybrid):
1) Week 0–1: Provision Dedicated reserved pool (small; 2x A10 sized nodes) in customer-preferred region. Configure private networking peering (customer VPC) and set up TLS + KMS integration for token encryption.
2) Week 1–3: Deploy a canary model (open small LLM with Redwood runtime). Run synthetic load to validate p95. Instrument cost and latency dashboards in Console.
3) Week 3–4: Integrate customer data flows (only passing pseudonymized artifacts through Redwood; any card PANs masked on-customer). Validate audit logs and access controls.
4) Week 4–6: Run live traffic shadowing and A/B run against hosted fallback (route low-confidence requests to hosted to compare latency/cost). Deliver final eval: latency report, cost per 1M tokens, and regression checks.

Sprint backlog (ordered, rough LOE, owner, ticket refs)
- SE-4123 Setup dedicated pool & infra peering (LOE 5d) - Owner: Ravi Singh - Jira SE-4123
- SE-4124 TLS/KMS integration + key rotation test (LOE 3d) - Owner: Maya Chen - Jira SE-4124
- SE-4125 Model packaging & performant config (quantization + batch tuning) (LOE 4d) - Owner: Leo Martinez - Jira SE-4125
- SE-4126 Console dashboards: SLO metrics, cost by route, KV cache effectiveness (LOE 2d) - Owner: Ava Thompson - Jira SE-4126
- SE-4127 Canary test harness + synthetic load script (LOE 3d) - Owner: Ravi Singh - Jira SE-4127
- SE-4128 Data flow gating & masking adapter (customer-side component) (LOE 4d) - Owner: Customer Eng (integration) - Jira SE-4128
- SE-4129 Fallback policy config (route to hosted during spikes) (LOE 2d) - Owner: Maya Chen - Jira SE-4129
- SE-4130 Final report & handoff docs (LOE 2d) - Owner: Ava Thompson - Jira SE-4130

Rough cost delta (very back-of-envelope)
- Hosted-only POC (approx): base usage 1M tokens -> $350 + variable. Pros: near-zero infra lead time. Cons: unpredictable if customer spikes and compliance concerns.
- Dedicated reserved POC (2 A10 nodes, 1 month reserved): approx $9k–12k (depends on commitment) + SE time. Predictable and lower per-token cost for high throughput.
- Private (on-prem) POC: minimal monthly provider cost but heavy SE+SRE time -> estimated $18k–25k total effort for initial onboarding.
Note: these ranges are intentionally wide; get detailed pricing sheet for firm numbers.

Risk register (top 6)
- R1: Customer cannot open necessary VPC peering in time -> mitigation: fall back to hosted demo with synthetic private masking. (Status: open)
- R2: KMS integration delays cause no access to encrypted logs -> mitigation: temp use of our audit-forwarding with obfuscation. (Status: open)
- R3: Model perf on quantized weights worse than expected -> mitigation: keep non-quantized canary in dedicated pool for baseline. (Status: open)
- R4: Unexpected traffic surge breaches p95 -> mitigation: pre-configured fallback to hosted lower-cost models and autoscaling alarms. (Status: open)
- R5: Customer legal requires additional contract SOW -> mitigation: involve contracts early; propose 30-day pilot terms. (Status: open)
- R6: Observability blind spots (missing trace hooks) -> mitigation: include tracing instrumentation in SE-4126. (Status: open)

Open questions for workshop (to resolve before kickoff)
- Q1: Will customer accept pseudonymization adapter (SE-4128) instead of sending tokens? (Action: product owner to confirm)
- Q2: Which region must Dedicated be provisioned in? (Action: ops to confirm)
- Q3: Are there internal SAML/SCIM requirements for console access during POC? (Action: security)
- Q4: Preferred fallback economic terms for hosted bursts (flat surcharge vs pay-as-you-go)? (Action: pricing)

Notes to self / quick meeting cheatsheet:
- Emphasize predictable cost benefit of Dedicated for monthly budgets.
- If customer timeline is < 2 weeks, plan for hosted first with data gating adapter.
- Keep Private as escalation path only — too slow for POC unless customer already has infra standing.
- Call out that dedicated pool sizing should start small; we can scale if metrics justify.

Appendix: quick links / references
- Small-kit sizing guide: confluence link above
- SE playbook for KMS: github PR 78 (infra-proposals)
- Sample contract addendum language (legal doc id: LEG-POC-2025)

Deliverables for customer at end of POC:
- Latency/cost SLO report (p50/p95/p99) by route and model
- Console export of token-level cost & traffic traces for 2 weeks
- Runbook for production handoff (recommended mode + scaling thresholds)
- Optional: proposal for Dedicated commit vs hosted usage price model (2 options)

Draft decision (for workshop vote):
- Move forward with Dedicated reserved pool + staged hosted fallback. If customer cannot provision peering within 10 business days, demo on-hosted with masking adapter and re-evaluate for Dedicated second wave.

-- end of draft --
